aldemar.headline: Munir flies to Tehran and the war premium drains — oil's worst day since the ceasefire died
aldemar.standfirst: Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir met President Pezeshkian in Tehran and Islamabad reported "significant progress", with both sides reviewing how to restore the June framework that lapsed on the 17th. Crude answered immediately: WTI fell 4.9% to 80.88, its worst session since the deadline passed, helped by a judgement that Monday's sanctions were milder than feared and by reports that barrels are still moving through Hormuz discreetly. Equities took the relief — S&P +0.32%, Nasdaq +0.66%, the 10-year down 6.5bp — but the Conference Board's confidence index fell to 89.4, its lowest since January. Dealer gamma flipped back positive with spot sitting almost exactly on the flip.

positions.title: 2 signals on BAC, INTC — read before the open

items.html: BAC — BAC +0.16% to 62.43 — a second close above 62, but consumer confidence just hit an eight-month low. The level has now held twice, which turns Thursday's break into confirmed noise: 62 is support again rather than a ceiling, with a 62.75 high and a 61.87 low that never threatened it. The problem is the other half of the thesis. Conference Board confidence fell to 89.4 from 90.2, the weakest since January, on worsening labour-market and inflation expectations — that is the third consecutive consumer datapoint pointing the same way after retail sales and Walmart. And the steepener idled again: the 10-year fell 6.5bp to 4.64%, so price is being held by rotation, not by margin. Gabriel −3.03% on entry at −0.49R, stop 60.39 3.4% below; Aldemar −2.70% at −0.38R, stop 59.65 4.5% below. Both stops untouched, both theses running on one engine instead of two — Jackson Hole is what restarts the other.

INTC — Chips rebound hard — Marvell +5.5%, AMD +4.6% — and INTC manages +0.25%. That gap is the information. When the sector bounces 5% and your name adds a quarter of a percent, the weakness is not sector beta any more; it is the $20B offering overhang doing what supply does, with $95 still overhead as the price the new holders paid. The 87.29 low held above Monday's 85.14, so a base is forming, but it is forming without help. Aldemar is −17.3% on entry at −0.74R, stop 81.10 now 7.3% below. Nvidia reports Wednesday — that print sets the whole complex's direction, and it is the single event most likely to decide whether this position ever gets back to its 142.75 target or finds the stop first.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.

themes.right: Munir mediation · "significant progress" · MoU restoration on the table
themes.title: The framework that died on the 17th is back on a table in Tehran

items.html: Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir meets Pezeshkian; Islamabad calls it "significant progress… a highly positive note". The agenda was explicit: prevent further escalation, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, end the conflict quickly. Both sides reviewed steps to restore the Islamabad MoU signed on 17 June — the same framework that expired last Monday. Pakistan brokered that one, which makes this the most credible channel open since the lapse.

Pezeshkian: "The United States must correct its tone and approach in dealing with Iran". Tehran is bargaining over posture rather than refusing to meet — a meaningful softening from last week's surrender-versus-total-settlement standoff. It is also a warning that Monday's sanctions campaign complicates the very deal Washington says it wants.

WTI −4.9% to 80.88 — sanctions read as milder than feared, and crude is still moving through the strait "discreetly". Three things drained the premium at once: the mediation, a market judgement that Operation Economic Outcast targets revenue rather than barrels, and evidence that substantial volumes still transit Hormuz off the books. Reports that Washington may return evacuated diplomats to the region added to the sense that escalation is less imminent.

themes.note: The transmission is oil → inflation → the regime call, and this is the first genuine reversal in three weeks: crude has now given back 8% from Thursday's high, which takes real pressure off the CPI path that has kept Policy tightening alive. Do not over-read it — Monday's brief made the point that with the strait already shut, oil now moves on diplomacy rather than on sanctions, and this is exactly that mechanic firing in the friendly direction. The asymmetry has flipped too: a failed Munir channel puts the premium straight back on, and it would land on a tape sitting on its gamma flip. Watch Islamabad, not Washington.

world.title: Relief rally with a rotting foundation: confidence at an eight-month low, and everything waits on Nvidia

items.html: Conference Board consumer confidence falls to 89.4 from 90.2 — the lowest since January. Labour-market and inflation expectations both deteriorated. Stack it on retail sales −0.6%, sentiment at 51 and Walmart's guidance cut and the consumer story is no longer a wobble — it is the clearest macro trend in the tape, and it sits underneath both BAC positions.

Dealer gamma flips back positive at +$5.2B with spot 7,677 sitting 0.06% above the flip at 7,672. Two sessions of amplification and the mechanic reverses again — but sitting this precisely on the flip is the least predictable place on the chart, not the safest. A point either side changes how every move behaves, and Nvidia's print arrives while spot is balanced on it.

Semis snap back — Marvell +5.5%, AMD +4.6% — as Nvidia's eve arrives with an employee charged over illegal chip exports to China. The complex bounced after a brutal fortnight, and the bar for Wednesday is now higher than it was at Monday's low. Nvidia has fallen seven straight sessions into its own print: positioning is short, which cuts violently in both directions on the number.

S&P +0.32% to 7,677, Nasdaq +0.66%, VIX −2.5% to 15.45; Dick's −26.1% on a miss and guidance cut, Moderna +10.5%. A quiet index number covering enormous single-name dispersion. Dick's losing a quarter of its value on retail guidance is the consumer theme arriving at individual desks — and it is the read-across worth watching for anything levered to discretionary spending.

weekly.headline: Gold's best week of the year against the book's hardest — and the war became the weather
weekly.standfirst: The week opened with a dead deadline and closed with a dead framework: the memorandum expired Monday, missiles landed off the UAE Tuesday, China-linked supertankers turned around Thursday, and by Friday Washington was asking a refusing Beijing to help sanction Tehran. Equities absorbed it slowly — the S&P lost 1.43%, chips roughly 10% as the AI-financing audit claimed Intel's $20B raise — while gold ran 6.6% to three records and crude added 5.4%. The book paid its first real tuition: Gabriel's INTC stopped out at exactly −1R on Tuesday, both BAC positions broke their 62 line after Walmart repriced the consumer, and GOOG quietly held the whole time. The market leaves the week in negative gamma for the first time all month.

The market stopped trading war headlines and started pricing a war baseline: Brent +5% on the week with acceleration, not spikes.CBS · Al Jazeera · Trading Economics · 17–21 Aug
TECHThe AI-financing audit claimed its biggest name: Intel's $20B raise at $95 → a 90.07 Friday close, chips −10% on the week. Dilution priced at a discount, marked below the offer within two sessions, and the whole complex re-rated with it. Add Wednesday's tepid OpenAI numbers and the audit now questions both how the build-out is funded and what it earns. Nvidia next week is the verdict.TradingKey · Trading Economics · 18–21 Aug
CONSUMERWalmart's guidance cut turned a data wobble into a confirmed slowdown — BAC broke its 62 line on the news. Retail sales −0.6%, sentiment 51, then the biggest retailer in the country blinked (−8.8% Thursday, −10% on the week). For a bank long the US consumer's balance sheet, the credit side of the thesis is now live risk, with the steepener side still intact against it.Eurasia Business News · Seeking Alpha · 14–20 Aug
METALSGold +6.6% — three records in five sessions, accelerating into strength. War premium, debt concerns, and a Treasury forced to buy its own long bonds: the debasement trade graduated from hedge to position. It was the single most profitable trade on the board this week, and nobody had to pick a stock to have it.Yahoo Finance · TradingKey · 17–21 Aug
NOISEFiled and ignored: target trims following Intel's share count, chart-pattern notes on BAC, a Pixel launch, an Alphabet retrospective. A full week of commentary that described moves after they happened. None of it changed a thesis, a level, or a size.various · 17–21 Aug

The discipline ledger matters as much as the P&L this week: Gabriel's INTC exit filled at exactly the planned 95.52 — a clean −1.00R, taken on schedule, with no slippage on a −6.6% day. That is the system doing precisely what it was built to do. The open book ends the week: Gabriel +0.79R on GOOG against −0.67R on BAC; Aldemar −0.55R on BAC and −0.64R on INTC, both inside their planned risk with stops standing.

sections.html:
From deadline to baseline: the week the war stopped being an event

TALKSMonday: the 60-day memorandum expires; Trump demands surrender and threatens Oman, the mediator. The only structure containing the conflict lapsed with neither side asking for more time. Everything after followed from this.17 Aug
STRIKETuesday–Wednesday: two Iranian missiles land off the UAE; a strait vessel struck, one casualty; Trump denies Kushner's "active conversations". The theatre widened to Gulf-state waters and the diplomatic track was publicly cut down by its own side within a day.18–19 Aug
SHIPPINGThursday: three China-linked supertankers turn back; UAE moves toward sanctions; transits hold near −19.5%. The strait's closure became physical for every flag, and the neighbourhood began picking the American side of the squeeze.20 Aug
POLITICSFriday: Washington vows its toughest sanctions and asks China — Beijing refuses; Iran and Oman quietly resume Hormuz talks. The economic escalation launched without its key enforcer, while the only de-escalation channel of the week opened in Muscat. Both facts are live into Monday.21 Aug

Oil ended the week at 86.86 WTI (+5.4%) with Brent's $93 handle intact, gasoline reached the US voter, and gold's record run said the hedgers expect neither loop to break. The regime consequence is direct: CPI y/y at 3.3 against the 2.5 floor stays propped open by energy, keeping Policy tightening alive into its sixth week. The single scenario that unwinds all of it — a Muscat framework — went from nonexistent to embryonic on Friday.

Unpinned, into Jackson Hole and Nvidia

GAMMAMonday opens the first negative-gamma tape of the run — net −$2.2B, spot below the 7,680 flip. Dealers amplify instead of dampen from here: wider ranges, live stops, trends that carry. Both BAC stops sit 2–4% away on a tape that just got faster — no position needs adding, every level needs respecting.Mon 24 Aug
FEDJackson Hole symposium — Powell speaks with $93 Brent against a cracking consumer. The rate path has to choose which problem it fears more. A hawkish lean lands on an unpinned tape; a dovish one feeds the gold trade. Either way it is the macro event of the week.late week
EARNINGSNvidia reports — the AI audit's verdict from the one desk that sees all the order books. After a week of chips −10%, Intel below its offer price, and tepid OpenAI numbers, guidance here either arrests the de-rating or accelerates it. Aldemar's INTC is a direct passenger.next week
LEVELSThe levels that decide the book. BAC: stops 60.39 (Gabriel) and 59.65 (Aldemar) below, 62 overhead — reclaim it and Thursday's break reads as expiry noise. INTC: the 89.75 week low against the 81.10 stop, with 95 the trapped-longs line overhead. GOOG: 340 reclaimed, watch the fresh gamma map Monday.Mon 24 Aug

Two positions sit in planned drawdowns with stops standing, one sits in profit, and the realized column already holds a clean −1R. Nothing about next week asks for a decision before the levels do — the work is letting a faster tape come to them.
